title: Michelin Star Restaurants in Seattle: Are There Any?
description: Seattle has no Michelin star restaurants, as no MICHELIN Guide covers Washington State. Why, how its restaurants are rated, and the nearest stars.
h1: Are There Michelin Star Restaurants in Seattle?
summary: Why Seattle and Washington State have no Michelin stars, how the city’s best restaurants are rated instead, and the nearest starred tables in Vancouver.
body:
No. There are no Michelin star restaurants in Seattle, or anywhere in Washington State, because no MICHELIN Guide covers Washington or Oregon, and Michelin hasn’t announced one. The nearest Michelin-starred restaurants are about 120 miles (190 km) north, across the border in Vancouver.

That surprises a lot of visitors, because Seattle is one of America’s great cities to eat in, from Pike Place Market oysters to Pacific Northwest tasting menus. The reason is simply where Michelin has chosen to go. Here is which parts of the US the guide does cover, why Seattle isn’t one of them, how the city’s best restaurants are judged instead, and where to find the nearest stars, with their prices.

Does Seattle have a MICHELIN Guide?

No. Michelin only awards stars in the places it publishes a guide for, and none of its American guides reaches Washington or Oregon. In the US it covers New York, Chicago, Washington DC, Boston and Philadelphia (one Northeast Cities guide since 2025), California, Florida, Texas, Colorado, the American South and, since August 2026, a Southwest guide for Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico and Utah. In April 2026 it announced a seventh region, the American Great Lakes, whose first stars come in 2027.

We checked the MICHELIN Guide’s own listings on 9 October 2026: it lists no restaurant at all within 150 km (about 95 miles) of Seattle, not even a Bib Gourmand. Portland is in the same position: there are no Michelin star restaurants in Washington State or Oregon, and there has never been a Seattle Michelin star.

Why there’s no Seattle guide yet

Each new guide is a business decision for Michelin, and most of its recent American guides have launched through partnerships with local or state tourism bodies that help pay for them. When the Great Lakes guide was announced, for example, Axios reported that Visit Indy had signed a three-year deal and was paying $150,000 in its first year. Michelin says such partners only help with marketing and promotion, and that its anonymous inspectors choose the restaurants independently.

No such deal has been announced for a MICHELIN Guide in Seattle or Washington State. Some Seattle critics see the funding model as the main reason the city has been left out: in September 2025 Seattle Met described the guide as a pay-to-play publication. Whatever the reason, the effect is the same. Without a guide, there are no inspections, and without inspections, there are no stars.

How Seattle’s best restaurants are rated instead

The awards that matter most in Seattle are the James Beard Awards, America’s best-known prizes for chefs and restaurants, which group Washington with Oregon, Alaska and Hawaii in their Best Chef: Northwest & Pacific category. In 2026 two Seattle chefs reached the final five: Aaron Tekulve of Surrell, a Pacific Northwest tasting-menu restaurant, and Johnny Courtney of Atoma. The prize went to Portland, to Ryan Roadhouse of Nodoguro. The last Seattle winner was Brady Williams in 2019, then the chef at Canlis, the city’s best-known fine-dining room, which has looked out over Lake Union since 1950.

Lists like these aren’t Michelin stars, and they don’t work the same way: the James Beard Awards are voted on by a panel of judges, while Michelin’s inspectors eat anonymously and decide as a team. But they’re the best guide to the restaurants Michelin would likely start with, if it ever came.

Where is the nearest Michelin star restaurant to Seattle?

Vancouver. The MICHELIN Guide has covered the city since 2022, and its fifth selection, on 6 October 2026, gives it {{in_vancouver}} starred restaurants ({{split_vancouver}}). The two-star is AnnaLena in Kitsilano, promoted that day, where the tasting menu costs {{dinner:annalena}}. The cheapest starred dinner menu in the city is at {{from_vancouver}}, and the full list, with lunch and wine pairing prices, is on our page for Michelin star restaurants in Vancouver.

From downtown Seattle, Vancouver is about three hours by car, plus the border crossing at Blaine, or around four hours on the Amtrak Cascades train. A dinner there makes an easy weekend: most of the city’s starred restaurants are open only for dinner, so book for the evening and stay the night. Beyond Vancouver, the next nearest stars are in Northern California, about 680 miles (1,100 km) south: see our page for San Francisco, a two-hour flight away.

Wherever you are in Washington, Near me lists every starred restaurant within the distance you choose, nearest first, with their prices.

Will Seattle ever get Michelin stars?

Michelin hasn’t said. Its international director, Gwendal Poullennec, has said that a new guide is always a process of several years, because inspectors need to see openings and consistency first, and that they scout far more destinations than ever get a guide. The pattern of the last few years, with Texas, Colorado, the American South, the Southwest and now the Great Lakes added one by one, shows Michelin is still expanding across the US.

If Michelin announces a Pacific Northwest guide, we’ll update this page straight away, and add a Seattle page with every starred restaurant’s dinner, lunch and wine pairing prices as soon as the first selection is out. Our calendar of MICHELIN Guide ceremonies shows when every guide reveals its stars.
